author: StarTalk
description:
Make it yourself at lovable.com

Are we in the center of the universe? Or does it just feel like it sometimes? Neil deGrasse Tyson and comedian Jordan Klepper tackle a grab bag of fan questions on curiosity, conspiracy, and cosmology. 

They start with why we use the word “queries,” why kids are such natural experimenters, and why facts alone rarely change minds. Jordan recalls interviewing a January 6 pardon recipient, Neil shares a moon landing skeptic story, and they discuss why trust is so hard to build. Is curiosity a choice or a trait?

Are we in the center of the universe? We explain the cosmic microwave background and how it reveals our motion toward Andromeda. Learn about the mass-giving property of the Higgs boson, why it’s called the “God particle,” and Jordan’s improv lessons for particle physicists. Is political unrest a function of political entropy? title: Neil & Jordan Confront Conspiracies | Cosmic Queries #116
